content.thinking:
I'm planning the composition carefully: a red panda with a ~0.6m body crouched atop a mossy boulder, one paw raised for balance, tail curving up behind it in an S-shape, all sized and posed to read clearly from the front.

Still working out proportions and joint placement...

For coloring, I'm planning the red panda palette: rust on the back, dark brown/black belly and legs, white face markings, and a ringed tail swept upward and curved via a tapering sweep path, with alternating dark/light rings based on position along the tail length.

Now I'm working out the head shape and facial coloring, defining the head center and sphere scale so I can mask cream/white cheek and muzzle regions using local coordinates relative to that head position.

Placing the eye decals at the sides of the head with small white eyebrow dots above, keeping cheeks and muzzle cream against the rust forehead. For the legs, I'm sketching dark capsule shapes from shoulder to paw and hip to paw, with the front-left leg raised through a shoulder-elbow-paw bend, and flattened dark spheres for the paws.

For claws I'll add three tiny cream spikes per paw, skipping toe beans for simplicity. For the moss-covered stone, I'm mottling the paint with grey and green, then scattering small flattened spheres across the upward-facing surface to form moss clumps, and layering in grass-blade card textures leaning at an angle for added texture.

Now I'm adding fur details: cheek tufts scattered on the sides of the head using cream triangle textures leaning outward and backward, plus body fur tufts scattered more densely across the rust-colored torso. I'm keeping the density moderate so it doesn't look too busy, and starting to plan the painted edge detailing along the body's lower boundary.

For the body shape, I'm switching to a tapered sweep along a smooth path with a varying radius array to get a more pear-like silhouette, colored in the rust tone. Legs will be a solid dark color, keeping things simple rather than adding extra shoulder accents.

For extra details, I'm adding a dark chest bib, a few smaller mottled stones around the base, maybe a small fern or flower accent, and some faint glowing floating motes nearby for a touch of whimsy, keeping everything grounded and within scene bounds.

I'm also sketching in a gold filigree bell tassel necklace around the neck using a small torus for the loop with a bell sphere and red tassel, tilting its orientation to sit naturally against the neck.

Setting up the builder structure with the necessary imports, then mapping out part positions for haunches and legs using mirrored loops across both sides of the body.

Now I'm working through the geometry math for the paw and stone placement, calculating where the leg meets the stone surface by solving for the sphere's height at specific x/z coordinates to make sure the foot sits flush.

Then I'm positioning the front legs and paws on both sides, placing one paw flat against the stone and the other leg raised toward the face with its rod, elbow, and forearm joints angled upward.

Still placing facial details...

Writing sweep and decal code...

Now I'm sketching texture cards for fur tufts and whiskers, using tinted SVGs for the neck ruff and grass blades, plus scattered moss spheres with mottled coloring on the stone surfaces.

Still defining materials and glow details...

Adding two more small rocks and figuring out overall proportions—panda body plus tail totaling around 0.55 length seems reasonable. Now I'm plotting the tail's curved path with position and radius keyframes, noting it extends beyond the stone's footprint so I'll need to handle that overlap.

I'm writing the paint function for the tail's ringed coloring, alternating rust and cream-rust bands with a dark tip, then moving to set up the amber anime-style iris for the eyes.

Switching the iris to a deep brown with lighter highlights to match a red panda's coloring. I'm scattering body fur cards based on surface normals, and now writing the head paint logic to define facial markings—cream cheek patches versus the base fur color based on position on the face.

Still writing head paint logic...

For the body, I'm applying a furEdge gradient from rust to dark, careful not to double-wrap cel. I'm pulling in animeEye, cel, furEdge, and INK from the toon kit, planning to use INK as the dark tone for the nose.

Now I'm checking which imports I'll actually need—THREE, createBuilder, catmull, rng, mottle, noise, paint, svg, glow—and working out how to use catmull for sweeping paths and drape for the fur strands, plus setting up sticks with the right geometry and color.

Writing flower petal code...
